narrative:
The model estimated a 25.0% probability that you would be a bad credit risk, meaning roughly a one-in-four chance of serious repayment difficulty. That does not mean default is certain, but under the bank’s approval rule this estimated risk was still above the cutoff, so the application was denied.

The strongest influence on the decision was the short requested term: nine months versus an approved-applicant average of about nineteen months. This worked in your favor and lowered the assessed risk. The second strongest influence was the business purpose of the loan; business loans are only 8.7% of approved cases, and this factor also lowered your assessed risk. The third strongest influence, and the main factor pushing the other way, was your checking-account status of 0–200 DM. Approved applicants most often have no overdrawn or low-balance checking status (59.2%), while only 18.4% are in the 0–200 DM group, so this feature raised the risk assessment. Overall, the favorable term and purpose signals were not enough to offset the risk signal from your checking-account position and the rest of your profile.

To improve your chances, focus on reducing the concern raised by your checking-account balance, provide evidence of stable cash flow and savings, and ask the lender what specific account-balance or documentation threshold would make a future application acceptable.
